items.title: Two cups, two ratios
items.instruction: Brew the same coffee twice at two different ratios — try 1:15 and 1:17 — and compare the taste side by side.

items.title: Blind process test
items.instruction: Brew a washed and a natural of the same origin, then taste blind and guess which is which.

items.title: Light vs dark, same origin
items.instruction: Brew a light and a dark roast of a coffee you like and notice which one you reach for again.

items.title: One-step grind test
items.instruction: Brew the same coffee twice, one grind step apart, and taste which side extracts better.

items.title: Fix one bad cup
items.instruction: Next time a cup is off, name it — sour and thin, or bitter and dry — and make exactly one change to fix it.

items.title: Name the origin
items.instruction: Next time you open a bag of coffee, find the country it was grown in — and say it out loud.

items.title: Compare two roasts
items.instruction: Brew a light and a dark roast side by side and notice which tastes brighter and which tastes bolder.

items.title: Move one grind step
items.instruction: Change your grinder by one step, brew again, and see whether the cup moves the way you expected.

items.title: Dial your ratio
items.instruction: Brew your usual cup, then brew it again with a little more coffee. Notice which one you like better.

items.title: Blind decaf test
items.instruction: Brew a decaf and a regular coffee, then taste them blind and see whether you can actually tell which is which.

items.title: Fresh vs pre-ground
items.instruction: Grind half your dose now and leave the other half ground overnight. Brew both the same way tomorrow and taste them side by side.

items.title: Brew it by the numbers
items.instruction: Brew one cup with a scale, a ratio and a timer — exactly as the lesson lays out. Just once, properly.
